children: Our Bureau Mumbai: The foreign currency non-resident bank [FCNR(B)] deposits mobilised by banks under special window stood at $132.9 billion, from the previous update of $127 billion, according to inflows reported by banks as of September 18. Taking into account the total inflows coming via external commercial borrowings (ECBs) and overseas foreign currency borrowings (OFCBs), the total inflows came in at $143.5 billion, according to data released by the RBI on Monday.

This is over five times the $26 billion raised under a similar scheme in 2013. Banks mobilised more money in the last 10 days of the scheme than they did in the first 74 days. Banks had raised $65.4 billion in the first 74 days. "We expect the total inflows to go up to $160 billion by the end of December because the RBI is still providing the hedging facility," said Gaura Sengupta, chief economist at IDFC First Bank. "Therefore, PSUs, for whom the scheme is largely for, may go ahead and borrow despite high global rates if they have targets." Over 5x of forex raised in 2013 window

title: Special Swaps Rake in $143.5b Deposits
